events.label: before creation
events.text: "then there was neither being nor non-being." the creation hymn of the rigveda asks how it all began, and ends: perhaps even the one who watches from the highest heaven does not know

events.label: the dawn of a kalpa
events.text: vishnu sleeps on the great serpent shesha, floating on the cosmic ocean. a lotus grows from his navel, and on it brahma is born and creates the worlds

events.label: every day of brahma
events.text: a day of brahma, a kalpa, lasts 4.32 billion years, and his night as long. at night the worlds dissolve; at dawn they are made again. after a hundred years of such days, all dissolves and a new brahma is born

events.label: the first flood
events.text: vishnu, as the fish matsya, warns manu of a great flood and tows his boat to safety with the seeds of all life and the seven sages

events.label: satya yuga: 1,728,000 years
events.text: the age of truth. dharma stands firm on four legs; people are good, wise, and live very long lives

events.label: treta yuga: 1,296,000 years
events.text: dharma stands on three legs. rama, the seventh avatar of vishnu, rescues his wife sita from the demon king ravana: the story of the ramayana

events.label: dvapara yuga: 864,000 years
events.text: dharma stands on two legs. krishna, the eighth avatar, is born; he guides arjuna in the great war at kurukshetra, and his teaching becomes the bhagavad gita

events.label: 3102 bce, by tradition
events.text: krishna leaves the world and the kali yuga begins: the age of strife, 432,000 years long, in which we live now
the indus cities flourish; some of their seals show figures in yoga-like poses, but how they relate to later hinduism is debated
the hymns of the rigveda are composed in early sanskrit and passed down by memory, word for word, for many centuries
the upanishads explore the self (atman), ultimate reality (brahman), karma, and rebirth
the great epics, the mahabharata and the ramayana, take their final form; the bhagavad gita becomes part of the mahabharata
in the gupta age, the puranas are written, and the first stone temples to vishnu, shiva, and the goddess are built
tamil poet-saints, the alvars and nayanars, sing of loving devotion (bhakti) to vishnu and shiva
adi shankara teaches that the self and brahman are one (advaita), and founds monasteries at the four corners of india
ramanuja teaches that loving devotion to vishnu leads to liberation
the khmer king suryavarman ii builds angkor wat in cambodia, a vast temple to vishnu
chaitanya leads ecstatic singing of krishna's names in bengal; in rajasthan, mirabai writes songs of love for krishna
tulsidas begins the ramcharitmanas, a retelling of the ramayana in hindi, still recited across north india
ram mohan roy founds the brahmo samaj, calling for reform and the worship of one god
swami vivekananda speaks at the parliament of the world's religions in chicago, bringing hindu teaching to the west
india becomes independent as a secular republic; partition divides hindus and muslims with great bloodshed
a. c. bhaktivedanta swami prabhupada founds the hare krishna movement in new york

events.label: today
events.text: about 1.2 billion hindus live mainly in india and nepal; the kumbh mela, held every twelve years at prayagraj, is often called the largest gathering of people on earth

events.label: the end of the kali yuga
events.text: kalki, the tenth avatar of vishnu, will come on a white horse to end the age of darkness, and a new satya yuga will begin

people.name: manu
people.about: saved from the flood by vishnu as a fish; the laws of manu are named after him

people.name: vyasa
people.dates: the end of the dvapara yuga, by tradition
people.about: said to have arranged the vedas and told the mahabharata, in which he also appears

people.name: valmiki
people.about: a robber turned sage who composed the ramayana, called the first poem

people.name: rama
people.role: prince of ayodhya and avatar of vishnu
people.about: the model of a righteous ruler, who defeats ravana to rescue sita

people.name: sita
people.about: honored for her courage and faithfulness while held captive in lanka

people.name: hanuman
people.about: rama's devoted helper, who leaps across the sea to find sita; a symbol of strength and loyalty

people.name: krishna
people.about: a playful cowherd, a hero, and the teacher of the bhagavad gita; for many hindus the supreme god himself

people.name: arjuna
people.about: his doubts before the battle of kurukshetra lead to krishna's teaching in the gita

people.name: adi shankara
people.about: taught advaita vedanta, the oneness of the self and brahman, and traveled all over india

people.name: ramanuja
people.about: taught that the soul is real and distinct, and is saved by loving devotion to vishnu

people.name: chaitanya
people.about: spread devotion to krishna through chanting and dancing in the streets

people.name: mirabai
people.about: defied her royal family to devote her life to krishna; her songs are still sung

people.name: tulsidas
people.about: wrote the ramcharitmanas, the best-loved book in north india

people.name: ram mohan roy
people.about: founded the brahmo samaj and campaigned against the burning of widows

people.name: ramakrishna
people.about: taught that all religions are different paths to the same god

people.name: swami vivekananda
people.about: a follower of ramakrishna who brought vedanta and yoga to the west

people.name: mahatma gandhi
people.about: drew on the bhagavad gita for his teaching of non-violence and truth

people.name: a. c. bhaktivedanta swami prabhupada
people.about: went to new york at 69 and founded the international society for krishna consciousness

glossary.definition: the true self or soul, which is not born and does not die.
a god coming down to earth in bodily form. vishnu has ten main avatars, including rama and krishna.
"the song of the lord": krishna's teaching to arjuna in the mahabharata, on duty, devotion, and the self.
loving devotion to a personal god, such as vishnu, shiva, or the goddess.
the ultimate reality behind everything, of which all gods are forms.
the right order of things, and each person's duty within it.
the festival of lights in autumn, celebrating the victory of light over darkness and rama's return home.
a day of brahma: 4.32 billion years, made of a thousand cycles of the four yugas.
the law that every action has consequences, in this life or the next.
liberation from the cycle of rebirth, the highest goal of life.
the sacred sound said at the start of prayers, seen as the sound of brahman.
worship, at home or in a temple, with offerings of flowers, food, light, and incense.
the endless cycle of birth, death, and rebirth.
the three great gods: brahma the creator, vishnu the preserver, and shiva the destroyer and renewer.
philosophical texts at the end of the vedas, about the self and ultimate reality.
the oldest scriptures, hymns and rituals in sanskrit, believed to have been heard by ancient seers.
"joining": paths of discipline of body and mind that lead toward union with the divine.
one of four ages in each cycle of time: satya, treta, dvapara, and kali, each shorter and darker than the last.
